precision.title: 24-hour automatic learning
precision.description: After installation, SignalCraft spends a day learning each machine's normal vibration and noise patterns, then sets its own baseline.

edge.title: AI handles the judgment calls
edge.description: No manual threshold tuning. AI tells normal from abnormal on its own, so operators can focus on running the site.

nonInvasive.title: Power on, scan QR, done

scalability.title: From reports to action in one place

detail.title: Why SignalCraft?
detail.subtitle: No complex graphs. Just clear equipment status anyone can understand.
detail.beyondTitle: It starts with learning what normal looks like
detail.beyondDesc: SignalCraft listens to each machine's sound and vibration for the first 24 hours and builds a baseline. That makes every alert and status check afterward more accurate and less noisy.
detail.edgeDesc: Instead of raw frequency charts, you get simple statuses like 'Normal / Caution / Alert', daily summaries, and failure-sign highlights that anyone on the team can read.

Footer.description: AI reads your facility's condition and sends daily reports, so you spend less time worrying about maintenance.

installation.q: Do I need to configure a lot up front?
installation.a: Nope. Plug it in, scan the QR code, and you're set. It learns the normal pattern on its own over the first 24 hours.

accuracy.q: When do alerts and reports start?
accuracy.a: Right after the learning period wraps up. You'll start seeing status cards, anomaly alerts, and daily summaries.

security.q: What data does SignalCraft use to judge status?
security.a: Vibration and noise patterns, runtime data, and past anomaly events. It pulls all of that together into a condition summary and daily reports.

environment.q: Can it be used beyond unmanned stores?
environment.a: Yes — it works just as well in small factories, building facilities, and other equipment environments.
